source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building accessibility checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
List the specific location of the failed check (e.g., main entrance, restroom, etc.).
3. Describe the accessibility issue in detail.
4. Use clear language to identify the exact violation against the accessibility standards (e.g., ADA, local building codes).
5. Include photographs or sketches of the issue, marking the areas of concern.
6. Record any measurements taken (e.g., width of door, height of countertop).
7. Note the exact standard(s) that the building is not compliant with (e.g., ADAAG, IBC).
8. Record the date and time of the inspection.
9. List the inspectors or assessors involved in the inspection.
10. Document any discussions or feedback from the building owner or caretaker regarding the issue.
11. Include potential solutions or recommendations for rectifying the issue.
12. Sign and date the report.
13. Attach any additional documents or forms pertinent to the failed check.
14.
